questions.context: QUESTION 1: INTERNAL CONTROL AND VAT (25 marks; 20 minutes) | 1.1 INTERNAL CONTROL. Read the following scenario and answer the questions that follow. Lennox High's Grade 10 learners have been running a small tuck-shop business at school during break time. They are a group of five who help each other at the tuck-shop. They have been recording everything they do. They kept their stock in an unlocked cupboard in the accounting teacher's classroom. Their cash was put in a shoe box and also put inside that cupboard. Two weeks after beginning their project, they were disappointed to notice that their trading stock and cash were missing. They have asked one of the Grade 12 Accounting learners to look at their books and check how much their loss is.
questions.text: The Grade 12 learner acts as their (internal / external) auditor.
Recommend THREE control measures or procedures that should be implemented in order to protect the trading stock and the cash from being stolen.
questions.memo_answer:
TRADING STOCK (any valid answer, three):
• Keep trading stock in locked storage space at all times
• Only one learner has the key to the storage space
• Do regular stock counts to match sales with cash received
CASH (any valid answer, three):
• Cash should be kept in a suitable and lockable money box
• Cash should be kept in a locked storage space / safe
• Cash should be banked regularly

questions.context: 4.3 INTERNAL CONTROL M Snook is employed by NT Traders. It is her duty to order stock, to record all transactions relating to these orders and to pay the suppliers. She frequently buys stock from regular suppliers for the personal use of the owner and staff members. She is too busy with her other duties to do the quarterly stocktaking as requested.
questions.text: Name and explain the GAAP principle that should be applied in the above scenario.
questions.memo_answer:
Business entity
Transactions of owner should be kept separate from that of the business and should be recorded as drawings.

questions.text: NT Traders do not have proper control of their trading stock. Identify THREE areas of concern and give a solution for each.
questions.memo_answer:
Area of concern -> solution:
• M Snook has too many responsibilities relating to ordering and recording of stock and payment of suppliers -> division of duties
• Stock ordered for personal use of owner and staff members -> transactions of the owner should be entered as drawings and staff members may only place orders with the necessary permission
• Regular stocktaking is not done -> stock must be counted on a regular basis; appoint more staff to assist M Snook

questions.text: It has been noted that the quality of the trading stock supplied by one of the regular suppliers has deteriorated. Give ONE suggestion as to how NT Traders can overcome this problem.
questions.memo_answer:
Any valid answer
Discuss the matter with the supplier
Find another supplier with better quality
